rows.direct_or_derived: Direct predicate output; inputs include model state and topology identities.
runtime_action: bracket/refine if detector uncertainty is numerical
stop affected scope before invalid topology use
rows.could_share_state: A process-state vector may inform the predicate; it does not itself define topology application.
rows.authority_note: Requires topology event coverage and transition mapping authority; does not assume the same authority closes other blockers.

rows.direct_or_derived: Directly evaluated from evolved process state, law and approved forcing.
runtime_action: stop or request successor model at validity boundary
rows.could_share_state: The process state may also feed interface/topology predicates; shared input does not prove a common authority.
rows.authority_note: Requires explicit process evolution law and validity scope.

rows.direct_or_derived: Requires model output mapped to declared interface support; rigid kinematics alone is insufficient.
runtime_action: record bracketed event candidate or preserve UNKNOWN
rows.could_share_state: May consume process state and approved kinematics; still requires its own response and event semantics.
rows.authority_note: No segment boundary type, polarity, or uniform response is inferred.

rows.direct_or_derived: Derived from topology/interface predicates under explicit membership rules; membership changes are not automatic.
runtime_action: stop affected consumers when validity is unknown/false
rows.could_share_state: May reuse topology/interface evidence, but support semantics and remapping authority remain distinct.
rows.authority_note: Topology-event coverage informs support validity; one shared causal authority is not presumed.

nonclosure_rule: This matrix defines model-interface evidence required to make blockers dynamically assessable. It does not claim the blockers are closed, independent, or covered by one authority; a common authority is not presumed. It does not select a model/provider or authorize a timestep.
